config.note: Composed: british-ds-4 for the other passes; filler-words from british-jev-4 (jev-1.13.0, thinking off).

findings.note: The clause never names who should note this. The surrounding sentences give no actor for the noting.
The draft never says who forgot the combination, and the preceding sentence names the buyer, so the reader has to assume the actor rather than find it.
'Realization' names the act of realizing, and the clause's verb is the empty 'had come to'. The action is buried in the noun.

findings.quote: The decision to sell was made
findings.note: 'Decision' and 'made' are separated by the infinitive 'to sell', so the weak verb is 'was made' and the noun is 'decision'. The actor performing the action is absent from the clause.
'Evaluation' names the action, and 'carried out' is the empty verb supporting it. The noun conceals the act of evaluating.

findings.quote: After eleven years of sitting in morning traffic behind a school bus,
findings.note: The main subject 'I' is preceded by eighteen words. This is a late subject.

findings.quote: Municipal snow contracts in our city
findings.note: The previous sentences describe the narrator's walk up Carver Hill. This sentence opens on city snow contracts, an aside the following sentence resumes the hill route without.

findings.quote: an anchor that kept me moored
findings.note: Stock image. The moored-to-concerns picture supplies no mechanism and stands in for an account of what the car actually did.

findings.quote: the city opened up like a book
findings.note: Stock simile. It asserts an opening and a readability that the sentence never supplies.
Distinctive word repeats within two sentences, the first occurrence being the picturesque row of Victorian houses.

findings.quote: I left the house at six-forty. I reached the bottom of the hill by seven. I arrived at my desk with wet socks and a temper.
findings.note: Three consecutive sentences open with the subject and a past-tense verb ('I left', 'I reached', 'I arrived'), a template that adds no structure the content needs.

findings.quote: I pass a picturesque row of Victorian houses on Linden Street, then the picturesque old mill that someone has turned into flats.
findings.note: Repeated example: the second sight is built on the same structure and makes the same point as the first, that the speaker now notices buildings on foot.

Paragraph 2 refers to 'the top of the hill' and to the walk as a punishment before the reader has met either; the hill and the first winter are only introduced in the paragraph beginning 'The first winter was very hard.'
The draft never says who should note this; the sentence presents a framing of the comparison with no responsible party.

findings.quote: It was decided in 2023 that all changes would go through this process
findings.note: The draft never names who decided that all changes would go through the board process. The surrounding sentences name the board only as the body that meets and posts decisions, not as the decider here.
The draft never says who raised the concerns. If this is the board, a team, or managers, the reader cannot tell whose objection the proposal is answering.
The verb 'conduct' carries the action noun 'review'; the action is buried in the noun rather than expressed by the verb.
'determination' buries the action of determining behind the empty verb 'makes'.

findings.quote: Given the results of the pilot and what both teams told us in the May retrospective,
findings.note: The subject 'I' is preceded by 17 words of introductory matter before the main clause.
The word 'cumbersome' appears twice within three sentences; the first occurrence is in the preceding sentence about the checklist.
Doubled pair: 'full and complete' says one thing twice.

findings.quote: a toll booth on the highway to production
findings.note: A stock image of the board as an obstruction. It supplies no mechanism for the delays that the following sentences do not already state plainly.

findings.quote: Oversight would remain in place for the changes where it matters most, and that point should not be lost.
findings.note: Restatement of the same oversight point made twice in the preceding two sentences.

findings.quote: median wait from six days to under one
findings.note: This paragraph cites a pilot and a six-day baseline before either exists for the reader; the pilot is only identified in the paragraph beginning 'In March and April, the Payments and Search teams ran a pilot.' and the six-day wait is only explained in the paragraph beginning 'Today every production release needs a sign-off from the board.'
The verb 'made' carries the action noun 'decision', burying the verb 'decide'.
'Undertaking' buries the act of undertaking behind the empty verb 'given', and 'assessment' buries assessing behind 'carry out', leaving the clause with no working verb.
'Assessment' names the action of assessing, and the verb doing the work is 'carry out'.

findings.quote: In the weeks after the water went down and the loss adjuster had come round to photograph each and every room,
findings.note: Twenty-three words precede the subject 'Ellen'. The introductory clause runs to more than twenty-five words before the subject.

findings.quote: Flood warnings for Quay Street were not issued
findings.note: The draft never says who failed to issue the warnings; the responsible body is the actor the paragraph is about.
No promisor is named anywhere in the paragraph, so responsibility for the promise cannot be traced.
Doubled pair: 'each and every' says the same thing twice. The doubling adds no meaning.
'Sodden' repeats within two sentences; the first occurrence is in the previous sentence in the same paragraph.

findings.quote: The flood wall was built in 1962
findings.note: The previous sentences concern warnings, sandbags and the police closing the street; the flood wall is a new element introduced only by the loose word 'flood'.
The opening names a wave of support, which no earlier sentence in the paragraph mentions. The previous sentences are about the flood as a shock and the bakery as the street's heart.

findings.quote: For the street, the flood was a wake-up call.
findings.note: The sentence shifts to a generalising statement about the street's reaction after the previous sentence was about Ellen's Christmas orders; the following sentence returns to Ellen's own action, so the generalisation sits as an aside in the line.

findings.quote: Gluten development depends on water temperature
findings.note: The sentence opens on a general fact about gluten development, unrelated to the account of Tom driving for flour. The next sentence returns to Ellen and the hall, as if this aside were not there.

findings.quote: harder to put a price on
findings.note: Stock image standing in for the specific losses the draft never names. The figure gestures at an argument the paragraph does not make.
Stock image. The draft supplies no picture of what the bakery does for the street, so the claim sits on the cliché alone.

findings.quote: lit a fire under the council
findings.note: Stock image. The draft never says what the pressure consisted of or what the council did, so the cliché carries the causal claim.

findings.quote: the flood was a wake-up call
findings.note: Stock image standing in for an argument the draft never makes about what the street is supposed to do now. It is also an inanimate abstraction ('the flood') being credited with the act of waking someone.
The answering figure cannot hold with the wake-up call figure: a call is not something answered by a person who slept through it. The two-vehicle image breaks down and the literal claim disappears.
Restatement: the earlier sentence 'she stepped into water up to her ankles' and the sequence of damage already establish the extent, so the sentence announces a point the draft already made.

findings.quote: It was obviously a shock to the whole street.
findings.note: Restatement: an announced judgment that the following 'The bakery is the beating heart' and the support response already carry.

findings.quote: The flood affected many people on Quay Street in many different ways.
findings.note: Restatement: the two following sentences 'Some lost stock and some lost income' and 'It is difficult to overstate how much the flood affected' repeat the same point without adding a fact.

findings.quote: The flood affected many people on Quay Street in many different ways.
findings.note: Repeats the street-wide-impact claim already made at 'It was obviously a shock to the whole street' and adds no new development of it.

findings.quote: The insurance payment, when it came in August, covered the ovens but not the flour
findings.note: Breaks the flood-morning account begun at 'At a quarter past four on the ninth of March,' which resumes at 'She rang her son Tom, who lives two streets up the hill.' The August insurance outcome is unrelated to the material between them.
The noun 'observation' buries the verb 'observe', carried by the empty verb 'made'.
'expectation' is an action noun carried by 'There was', with the verb 'expect' available.
The noun 'determination' buries the verb 'determine', carried by 'made'.
The noun 'decision' buries the verb 'decide', and the clause's verb is the empty 'made'. The same action also appears earlier as 'It was decided'.

findings.quote: a decision would be made regarding the proposal.
findings.note: The clause does not name who would make the decision, and neither the clause nor the surrounding sentences identify that actor. The actor is responsible for the decision the paragraph is about.
The draft never says who would make the determination. The actor is the person or body responsible for the determination the text is about, and the reader cannot identify it.
"resolution" repeats within two sentences; the first occurrence is at the start of the paragraph.

findings.quote: It is a feeling that recurs.
findings.note: The template 'It is a feeling that' appears twice in consecutive sentences, first in 'It is a feeling that is familiar.'
'Feeling' is used three times across the three sentences, the first occurring in 'the feeling that nothing had been accomplished.'
'was arrived at' repeats verbatim within two sentences, following 'would be arrived at'.

findings.quote: It was decided by the committee that
findings.note: This paragraph repeats the ground of the paragraph opening 'It was decided by the committee thxt x determination would be made regarding the proposal' and adds nothing to it.

findings.quote: There was an expectation that a resolution would be arrived at
findings.note: This paragraph repeats the ground of the paragraph opening 'There was an expectation that' earlier in the draft and adds nothing to it.

findings.quote: Some of us left the room with the feeling
findings.note: This paragraph repeats the ground of the paragraph opening 'Some of us left the room with the feeling' earlier in the draft and adds nothing to it.
